newsitem.title: USA: Miami mayor lashes out at budget oversight board.
newsitem.headline: Miami mayor lashes out at budget oversight board.

text.p: Miami Mayor Joe Carollo lashed out at the state oversight board that rejected the city's financial recovery plan, saying board members had "taken things to an extreme," Miami Herald reported Thursday.
Carollo made the remarks on Miami's Spanish-language radio station WQBA on Wednesday, one day after the oversight board rejected the city budget.
"The people working on behalf of the state have gone too far," the newspaper quoted him as saying.

The board, appointed by the governor to oversee Miami's efforts to close a $68 million budget deficit, said the city plan contained $9.9 million in revenues that were questionable, including federal grants that are uncertain, overdue garbage fees the city will try to collect via liens and cost savings estimates the board called unrealistic.

The board also asked the city to set aside $13.6 million, or 20 percent of the estimated deficit, in reserves to cover any potential shortfall. The board gave the city until Jan 25 to make the revisions.
The Herald quoted Carollo as saying, "We were at the goal line, ready to carry in the touchdown. They changed the rules and said we had more than 20 more yards to go."
In fact, board members had previously said the city needed to set aside reserves but did not cite a dollar amount.
Carollo also said the state failed to provide budget experts or economic help to the city.
"No one gave us a cent," he said.

The state has loaned the city some budget experts and advanced Miami $22 million of tax revenues it otherwise would have received in monthly payments. But the governor said giving Miami a bail-out grant would only exacerbate the city's problems because it spends more than it takes in.
Carollo also complained that the board was trying to force the city to double its garbage fees to raise $10 million, something he insisted he would not allow.

"Every time the board meets, the only thing we see in the press the next day is they're saying the City Commisison doesn't have the political courage to raise the garbage fees," Carollo said. "If they think the city of Miami is like a punching bag that's only there to receive blows, that's not the city of Miami. The city of Miami does have people who are willing to make confrontations."
Board members have expressed concern that the city budget continued to subsidize garbage services with general fund revenues.
